events.title: CERN releases the web into the public domain
events.summary: CERN released the World Wide Web technology into the public domain on April 30, 1993 — no royalties, no licensing fees.
events.about: Berners-Lee and CERN's decision let anyone build browsers and servers without permission — enabling Mosaic, Netscape, Apache, and the commercial internet. It is one of the most consequential open releases in computing history.

narrative.whyChosen: Public-domain release unlocked the web's exponential growth.
narrative.whyImportant: It prevented proprietary lock-in on hypertext protocols.
narrative.problemSolved: Companies could have patented or licensed core web technology.

events.title: Jensen Huang co-founds NVIDIA
events.summary: Jensen Huang, Chris Malachowsky, and Curtis Priem founded NVIDIA on April 5, 1993 — starting as a graphics chip company that later powered AI.
events.about: NVIDIA's GPUs went from PC gaming to CUDA parallel computing to training virtually every large language model. Huang has been CEO since founding — one of the longest and most consequential runs in semiconductor history.

narrative.whyChosen: NVIDIA became the dominant AI compute platform of the 2020s.
narrative.whyImportant: GPUs shifted from graphics cards to the engine of deep learning and HPC.
narrative.problemSolved: 3D graphics needed dedicated parallel hardware beyond general-purpose CPUs.
